title: Textile cess and a borrowed definition

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I am Ravishankar from LawWorld. If a cess law does not define manufacture, can the revenue borrow the definition from the Central Excise Act?
Twenty sixth October, twenty twenty six: the Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice S V N Bhatti and Honourable Justice N V Anjaria ruled.
scenes.shown: 26 October 2026: the Supreme Court bench of Honourable Justice S.V.N. Bhatti and Honourable Justice N.V. Anjaria ruled.

scenes.dialogue: Section Five A of the Textiles Committee Act levies a cess on textiles manufactured in India, except those from the powerloom or handloom industry.
scenes.shown: Section 5A of the Textiles Committee Act levies a cess on textiles manufactured in India, except those from the powerloom or handloom industry.

scenes.dialogue: Premium Suiting dyes and bleaches man-made fabric for powerloom and handloom units, on job work. In two thousand one, the Committee's officer demanded cess from it.
scenes.shown: Premium Suiting dyes and bleaches man-made fabric for powerloom and handloom units, on job work. In 2001, the Committee's officer demanded cess from it.

scenes.dialogue: The Tribunal held the processing was manufacture. But in twenty thirteen, the Allahabad High Court quashed it: dyeing did not erase the fabric's powerloom status.
scenes.shown: The Tribunal held the processing was manufacture. But in 2013, the Allahabad High Court quashed it: dyeing did not erase the fabric's powerloom status.

scenes.dialogue: The Committee argued: its Act does not define manufacture, so use Section Two f of the Central Excise Act, which covers incidental processes.
scenes.shown: The Committee argued: its Act does not define manufacture, so use Section 2(f) of the Central Excise Act, which covers incidental processes.

scenes.dialogue: The Supreme Court disagreed. A word undefined in one Act cannot take another Act's definition, unless brought in by reference or incorporation.
Every statute has its own context. So manufactured in Section Five A takes its common parlance meaning, not a sense borrowed from another statute.
scenes.shown: Every statute has its own context. So "manufactured" in Section 5A takes its common parlance meaning, not a sense borrowed from another statute.

scenes.dialogue: The company's dyeing and bleaching on job work was not manufacture: at best, the textile was upgraded. So no cess was due, and the appeal was dismissed.
